info.description: Multi-tenant ELD / fleet management API. Every endpoint below /api/v1 requires a bearer access token unless it is marked `@x-permission public`.
info.title: ONEBOOK ELD API

get.description: Versioning gate for the mobile client: `min_supported_version`, `latest_version`, `force_update` and the deployment feature flags.

post.description: Q3.4 — mandatory for Super Admin and Administrator. The shared secret is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted and is only enabled once POST /auth/2fa/verify succeeds.
Q3.4 — confirming an enrolment returns the ten single use recovery codes exactly once and upgrades a limited token into a full session.
Q16 — the link is valid for 72 hours and only its SHA-256 hash is stored. Setting the password revokes every existing session of the account.

Q20 — one session per device_type: signing in on the same device type revokes the previous session and answers `replaced_session: true`. Super Admin and Administrator accounts without 2FA receive a limited token and `requires_totp_setup: true`.
Q3.1 — `pause: true` is Leave Truck: the session becomes `paused` and is resumed with POST /auth/pin/verify.
post.summary: Sign out or pause the session

post.description: Q16 — always answers 202 so the endpoint cannot enumerate accounts. A new link invalidates the previous one.
Q16 — the token works once. A successful reset revokes every session of the account.
Q16 — Switch driver / Return to truck. `return_to_truck` resumes the paused session. Five consecutive failures lock the PIN for 15 minutes.
Q3.1 — every refresh returns a new opaque token and invalidates the old one. Replaying a rotated token revokes the whole session and is audited as `token_reuse`.

get.description: Q20 — the caller's own non revoked sessions, one per device type. Addresses are truncated.

delete.description: Q20 — a session belonging to another user answers 404, never 403, so session ids cannot be probed.

get.description: TZ A§15 — the platform tenant list. Super Admin only: a company scoped principal receives 403.

post.description: TZ A§15 — provisions the tenant in one transaction: the company row, the FMCSA 70/8 default `hos_policy_versions` entry, a copy of the system roles with their permissions, the A§19 notification defaults, the Administrator account in `invited` state and its 72 h invitation. The invitation token is delivered out of band and never returned.

patch.description: Partial update from the platform console. An unknown or soft deleted company answers 404.

TZ A§15 — MVP billing is manual: the platform administrator extends `subscription_end_at` once the invoice is settled. `grace` covers the 7 days after the period ends, `readonly` freezes the admin panel while the driver app keeps recording HOS.

get.description: TZ A§1 — the tenant profile plus the region profile (region, unit_system, regulation_profile) and the company level settings document.

patch.description: Q0.1/Q0.2 — region, unit_system and regulation_profile drive the labels and the unit conversion in every client. Omitted fields are left unchanged; `settings` replaces the whole settings document.

get.description: Company locations used as the Sub Admin scope target.

delete.description: Soft delete. A branch that still has assigned users answers 409 RESOURCE_IN_USE.

patch.description: A branch of another tenant answers 404, never 403.

get.description: The audit_log rows of the caller's company. The client IP is never returned.
Q10.1 — the hos_policy_versions row whose effective_from is the latest one not in the future. A company without a stored version falls back to the FMCSA 70/8 defaults.

post.description: Q10.1 — a policy change is never retroactive: `effective_from` must not be in the past and days before it keep being evaluated with the previous version. Keys left out of `policy` inherit the currently effective value.
post.summary: Publish a new HOS policy version

get.description: TZ A§19 — one entry per alert type with its delivery channels and the recipient role ids. Alert types the company never customised are returned with the defaults of the specification table.

patch.description: Q89 — only the listed alert types are written; the rest keep their configuration. `channels` replaces the previous list, an empty list mutes the alert for every channel.

get.description: Q1 — paginated Driver Management list. Filters: status, branch_id, fleet_manager_id, search. `include_inactive=false` hides deactivated drivers. Branch scoped callers only ever see their own branch. `license_no` is never returned in clear text.

parameters.description: Name, username, email or phone fragment
parameters.name: search

post.description: Q18.1 — required: first_name, last_name, username (4-32 of [a-z0-9._]), license_no and at least one of email / phone (the invitation is delivered over it). **There is no password field**: a users row is created with the Driver role and status `invited`, and an invitation link is sent. `license_no` is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted and answered masked. Co-driver is optional.

get.description: Downloads the driver list as CSV (default) or XLSX. `license_no` is exported **masked**, never in clear text. Every download is recorded in `audit_log` (who exported what, TZ B§3.6).

post.description: TZ §18.4 — multipart upload of `drivers_import_template` (first_name, last_name, username, phone, email, license_no, license_region, home_terminal). Validation is row by row and **all-or-nothing**: one critical error and nothing at all is written; the body then lists every `{row, field, message}` and the response status is 422. Every imported driver gets a users row (Driver role, status `invited`) and an invitation link; `license_no` is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted.

get.description: TZ §18.4 — `drivers_import_template` with the exact column order the importer expects, plus one sample row.
Cross-tenant reads answer 404, never 403 (TZ B§3.5).

delete.description: Soft delete (`deleted_at`): the drivers row and its user account are archived and every session is revoked. Logs stay untouched.

patch.description: Partial update; omitted fields stay unchanged. Changing `license_no` re-encrypts the column. `status`, `company_id` and the role can never be set here.

post.description: Q1 — reversible transition back to `active`. A driver that never accepted the invitation keeps user status `invited`.

parameters.description: Optional reason for the audit trail
parameters.name: body

get.description: Every audited change of the driver and of its user account, its logins and its session state transitions, newest first. Sourced from `audit_log` and `sessions`.
TZ §1.1 — the pair is stored once but shown on both sides: if B is a co-driver of A, A also appears in B's list.

post.description: Q45 — creates one canonical `driver_pairs` row; the relation is symmetric. Re-linking a previously removed pair restores it instead of failing.

delete.description: TZ D§3 lists `DELETE /drivers/{id}/co-drivers`; the partner is named by the `co_driver_id` query parameter.
Soft deletes the `driver_pairs` row. The link disappears from both drivers.

post.description: Q1 — an inactive driver cannot sign in (`403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE`) and **every one of its sessions is revoked immediately**, so already issued access tokens stop working too.

parameters.description: Optional reason for the audit trail
parameters.name: body

get.description: TZ B§3.4 — `drivers.license_no` is stored AES-256-GCM encrypted. The list and the driver payload only ever carry `license_no_masked`; the clear value is served here and only to a caller holding `drivers.update`. Every call is answered from the encrypted column, never from a cache.

post.description: Q18.1 — a driver password is only ever set through an invitation, so "reset password" reissues the link (72 h, delivered by email or SMS). The previous link is burned and every live session is revoked. The token is never returned over the API.

get.description: Registered ELD hardware with its current unit, firmware and raised malfunction codes.

post.description: `(company_id, serial)` is unique among rows that are not soft deleted. Q3.1 — wiring the device to an inactive unit answers 409.

get.description: Cross-tenant identifiers answer 404, never 403.

delete.description: Soft delete; the open unit assignment is closed in the same transaction and the serial becomes reusable.

patch.description: Partial update; omitted fields keep their stored value.

post.description: Writes `eld_device_assignments` (from_at/to_at). A null `unit_id` detaches the device. One unit carries at most one active device (409 ALREADY_ASSIGNED) and Q3.1 forbids wiring to an inactive unit (409 INVALID_STATE).
post.summary: Wire an ELD device to a unit

post.description: TZ B§3.4 — the API never proxies bytes. `kind` is a closed whitelist (dvir_photo, invoice, signature, logo, chat, import); the content type and the size are checked against the per-kind ceiling (DVIR photo ≤ 5 MiB, invoice ≤ 10 MiB) before anything is signed. The object key is derived server side from the tenant, the kind and a random uuid — a client supplied path is never trusted — and only that key is stored. The URL is a PUT valid for 15 minutes and its `Content-Type` header is part of the signature.

get.description: Q82 — the signed in profile with its effective permission keys and scope. Never returns a password hash, a TOTP secret or a token.

Q82 — every RBAC key grouped by module with its description. Audit critical modules (logs, dvir, violations, telemetry, audit_log) deliberately have no `delete` key (Q82.2). Any authenticated session may read it; no dedicated permission is required.
Q81 — the system templates (`is_system: true`, shared by every company) plus the roles this company defined. System roles can be read but never edited or deleted.

parameters.description: Only system or only custom roles
parameters.name: is_system

post.description: Q82 — every permission key must exist in GET /permissions; unknown keys and any `delete` key of an audit critical module (logs, dvir, violations, telemetry, audit_log) are rejected with 422.

409.description: UNIQUE_VIOLATION — the role name is taken

delete.description: Q81 — soft delete. A role that still has users answers 409 ROLE_IN_USE; a system role answers 403 SYSTEM_ROLE_IMMUTABLE.

patch.description: Q81/B§3.1 — a system role answers 403 SYSTEM_ROLE_IMMUTABLE. Any change invalidates the cached permission set and revokes the sessions of every holder, so a narrowed role takes effect immediately.

post.description: `(company_id, number)` is unique among rows that are not soft deleted.

get.description: Q1/Q2 — only active units are returned unless `include_inactive=true`. A branch scoped principal always sees its own branch only. `odometer_m` is the last telemetry reading in metres; the backend never converts units.

post.description: Q18.1 — required: unit_number, make, model, license_plate, fuel_type. VIN is optional and validated as 17 characters when present. `(company_id, unit_number)` and `(company_id, vin)` are unique among rows that are not soft deleted.

get.description: Downloads the unit list as CSV (default) or XLSX. Every download is recorded in `audit_log`.

post.description: TZ §18.4 — multipart upload of `units_import_template` (unit_number, make, model, year, plate, plate_region, vin, fuel_type, sleeper_berth). Validation is row by row and **all-or-nothing**: one critical error and nothing at all is written; the body then lists every `{row, field, message}` and the response status is 422.

get.description: TZ §18.4 — `units_import_template` with the exact column order the importer expects, plus one sample row.
Cross-tenant and out of scope identifiers answer 404, never 403.

delete.description: Q1 — soft delete (`deleted_at`). Related logs, DVIR reports and telemetry are kept; the unit_number and VIN become reusable.

patch.description: Partial update; omitted fields keep their stored value. Renaming into an existing unit_number or vin answers 409.

post.description: Q1 — the active ⇄ inactive transition is reversible and audited.
Q1.1 — a unit holds one open assignment per role, so assigning a new `primary` closes the previous one. An inactive unit or driver answers 409.
post.summary: Assign a driver to a unit

post.description: Q3.1 — an inactive unit accepts no ELD connection and no driver assignment.

get.description: TZ §10.1/§10.5 — `connection_state` is Online when telemetry is younger than five minutes, Offline when it is older, Disconnected when the device reported the link is down and Malfunction when any FMCSA code (P/E/T/L/R/S/O) is raised. Telemetry values are raw: distance in metres, speed in km/h.
Q3 — the audit_log entries of the unit merged with its driver assignment history, newest first.
Q1/Q82.1 — a branch scoped caller only ever sees its own branch, whatever `branch_id` says. Never returns a password hash, a TOTP secret or a PIN.

post.description: Q81/A§16 — there is no password field: the account is created with status `invited` and a 72 hour invitation link is delivered by email or SMS. Either `email` or `phone` is required.

409.description: UNIQUE_VIOLATION — username or email already used

delete.description: Q1 — soft delete: `deleted_at` is stamped, related logs and DVIR records are kept. You cannot delete your own account, nor the last active Administrator of the company.

patch.description: Q82.1 — changing the role revokes every session of the account so the new permission set applies immediately. Activity state is changed with the activate / deactivate endpoints, not here.

post.description: Q1 — active ⇄ inactive is reversible. An account that has not accepted its invitation cannot be activated: resend the invitation instead.
Q3.1 — an inactive user cannot sign in (403 ACCOUNT_INACTIVE) and every session of the account is revoked immediately. You cannot deactivate yourself or the last active Administrator.
A§16 — a fresh 72 hour link is issued and the previous one is invalidated. The token itself is delivered out of band and never appears in the response.

409.description: INVALID_STATE — the invitation was already accepted

post.description: A§16 — an administrator never sets a password: this endpoint only re-sends a one time link, exactly like the invitation flow. An inactive account is rejected.

access_token_ttl_seconds.description: AccessTokenTTLSeconds lets a client schedule its refresh.

feature_flags.description: FeatureFlags toggles optional modules per deployment.

server_time.description: ServerTime lets the client detect clock drift before signing events.

support_email.description: SupportEmail is shown on the mobile about screen.

pin.description: PIN optionally sets the 6 digit driver PIN in the same call.

company_id.description:
CompanyID disambiguates a username that exists in several tenants. It is
a pre-authentication hint only: the effective tenant always comes from
the resolved user row, never from this field.

device_type.description: DeviceType decides which of the three concurrent session slots is used.

totp_code.description: TOTPCode is required once two factor authentication is enabled.

expires_in.description: ExpiresIn is the access token lifetime in seconds.

refresh_expires_at.description: RefreshExpiresAt is when the refresh window closes.

refresh_token.description: RefreshToken is empty while the session is limited to 2FA enrolment.

replaced_session.description:
ReplacedSession reports that another session of the same device type was
revoked by this login (TZ A§20).

requires_totp_setup.description:
RequiresTOTPSetup marks a limited token: the account must enrol in two
factor authentication before anything else is permitted.

session_id.description: SessionID identifies the session created by this login.

subscription_readonly.description:
SubscriptionReadonly reports that the company subscription lapsed and
only read operations are accepted.

pause.description: Pause keeps the session recoverable with a PIN (Leave Truck).

refresh_token.description: RefreshToken optionally targets one session explicitly.

session_resumed.description: SessionResumed reports that a paused session was reactivated.

action.description: Action selects what the verified PIN unlocks.

login.description: Login is the username or the email address of the account.

company_id.description: CompanyID is empty for platform (super admin) accounts.

email.description: Email is masked for anyone but the account owner.

ip.description: IP is truncated; the full address stays in the audit trail only.

digits.description: Digits and Period describe the expected authenticator configuration.

otpauth_url.description: OtpauthURL is rendered as a QR code by the client.

secret.description:
Secret is the base32 value for manual entry. It is shown once and is
stored AES-256-GCM encrypted.

recovery_codes.description:
RecoveryCodes are shown exactly once, at enrolment. Only their hashes
are stored and each code works a single time.

tokens.description: Tokens is filled when the verification upgraded a limited session.

recovery_code.description: RecoveryCode is accepted instead of Code when the device is lost.

expires_in.description: ExpiresIn is the access token lifetime in seconds.

refresh_expires_at.description: RefreshExpiresAt is when the refresh window closes.

refresh_token.description: RefreshToken is empty while the session is limited to 2FA enrolment.

channel.description: Channel selects how the invitation link is delivered.

username.description: Username defaults to the local part of the email address.

administrator_role_id.description: AdministratorRoleID is the company's copy of the Administrator role.

administrator_user_id.description: AdministratorUserID is the invited Administrator account.

invitation_channel.description: InvitationChannel is how the link was delivered.

invitation_expires_at.description: InvitationExpiresAt is when the invitation link stops working (72 h).

roles_created.description: RolesCreated is the number of system role templates copied.

subscription_end_at.description:
EndAt is the moment the paid period ends. Send null together with
clear_end_at to drop the date entirely.

effective_from.description:
EffectiveFrom must not be in the past: retroactive violations are
forbidden. Omitted means "now".

distance_regions_set.description:
DistanceRegionsSet selects the region catalogue used by the distance
report (Q0.1).

fuel_types.description: FuelTypes limits the values a unit may declare.

quick_notes.description: QuickNotes are the note presets offered on the duty status form (Q1.3).

co_driver_id.description: CoDriverID is optional (Q18.1) and creates a symmetric driver_pairs row.

filename.description: Filename is optional and only contributes a sanitised file extension.

size_bytes.description:
SizeBytes is the size the client is about to upload; it is checked
against the per-kind ceiling before a URL is issued.

malfunction_codes.description: MalfunctionCodes are the raised FMCSA Appendix A letters (P/E/T/L/R/S/O).

unit_id.description: UnitID is null to detach the device from its current unit.

eld_device_id.description: EldDeviceID is the ELD currently wired to this unit, null when none.

odometer_m.description:
OdometerM is the last telemetry odometer reading in metres, null when the
unit has never reported. The backend never converts units.

connection_state.description: ConnectionState is the administrator facing device state.

malfunction_codes.description:
MalfunctionCodes are FMCSA Appendix A letters: P power, E engine sync,
T timing, L positioning, R data recording, S data transfer, O other.

kind.description: Kind separates the two sources merged into one timeline.

permissions.description: Permissions are ordered exactly like the catalogue.

is_system.description: IsSystem roles (Super Admin, Administrator, ...) cannot be edited.

scope.description: Scope decides how far a holder of the role can see (TZ Q82.1).

permissions.description: Permissions must be keys of GET /permissions; unknown keys are rejected.

scope.description: Scope is company or branch; `self` is reserved for the built in Driver role.

permissions.description: Permissions replaces the whole set when present.

status.description: Status follows TZ Q1: invited -> active, active <-> inactive.

branch_id.description: BranchID is required for a branch scoped role.

channel.description:
Channel selects how the invitation is delivered; empty picks email when
an address is present, otherwise sms.

email.description: Email or Phone is required: it is the channel the invitation is sent on.

username.description: Username must be unique inside the company.

branch_id.description: BranchID accepts an explicit null to detach the user from its branch.
